ALLOCATION_COLLISION_SWEEP.method: Two independent sweeps. (1) A per-ref OBJECT-EXISTENCE sweep: for every ref returned by git for-each-ref over refs/heads and refs/remotes, git cat-file -e <ref>:docs/ops/ods/ODS_V1_MAINTENANCE_ADDENDUM_v1.0.36.json and, separately, a source inspection of <ref>:scripts/ods-scope.ts for a row literally carrying authorityId: 'HPO-ODS-W2-33'. (2) A tracked-file CONTENT sweep at this head classifying every textual occurrence of each candidate.
ALLOCATION_COLLISION_SWEEP.why_the_two_sweeps_are_both_needed: The content sweep sees text at THIS head only and cannot see a sibling candidate branch. The per-ref sweep sees every ref but sees only the allocating FORM - a blob at the addendum path, a registry row with the id. Together they close both "someone else already allocated it elsewhere" and "something at this head is an allocation I misread as prose".
ALLOCATION_COLLISION_SWEEP.why_the_ALLOCATING_FORM_is_what_is_swept: Both candidate identifiers have DOZENS of textual occurrences at this head, and every one of them is a prohibition or an absence assertion. A substring count is therefore worthless as a collision test: it would report a collision that does not exist. What makes an identifier ALLOCATED is a file at the addendum path carrying that version, or a PROTECTED_GRANTS row carrying that authorityId. Those are the forms that were swept.

protected_grant.THE_BRANCH_IS_NOT_CREATED_BY_THIS_ACT: The branch string is BOUND. The ref is NOT created, NOT moved and NOT modified by this mission. Binding a grant to a branch name that does not yet exist is the normal and correct shape: the grant resolves only when a gate runs FROM that branch, and until the implementation lane creates it, the grant resolves nowhere.
protected_grant.THE_GATE_READS_THE_BRANCH_FROM_THE_WORKI: Running the scope gate from a detached HEAD, or from a worktree on any other branch, resolves NO grant regardless of what --protected-authority names. There is no flag and no environment variable that overrides the branch the gate reads from the working directory. The implementation lane must therefore actually be on the bound branch.
protected_grant.grant_does_not_replace_allow: A resolved protected grant authorizes a protected path ONLY in combination with the ordinary --allow for that same path. The grant removes the PROTECTED violation; it does not remove the UNAUTHORIZED classification. The implementation writer must supply both --protected-authority HPO-ODS-W2-33 and an exact --allow for each of the two literals.
protected_grant.BOTH_PATTERNS_NAME_GENUINELY_PROTECTED_P: MEASURED. DEFAULT_PROTECTED_PATTERNS in scripts/ods-scope.ts contains db/prepared/**, and both literals sit underneath it. Neither is a path that would have passed without a grant, so neither pattern is decorative.

PATTERN_2_the_prepared_README.it_is_NOT_redundant_with_the_five_other_: MEASURED. FILESYSTEM_SENTINEL_DISPOSITION.why_this_section_exists: This act modifies one existing file, and the reason must be stated in terms of which predicates the new artifact falsifies - not in terms of a diff.
FILESYSTEM_SENTINEL_DISPOSITION.PRESTATE: tests/ods/ods-scope.test.ts carries the live LINEAGE-axis sentinels for this position: assertions that docs/ops/ods/ODS_V1_MAINTENANCE_ADDENDUM_v1.0.36.json does NOT exist, a dense-maximum pin at 35, and a corpus collision sweep asserting that no addendum carries version 1.0.36 or GRANT_ID HPO-ODS-W2-33. Creating this artifact makes every one of them FALSE.
FILESYSTEM_SENTINEL_DISPOSITION.THE_RED_POPULATION_WAS_MEASURED_NOT_INHE: BINDING METHOD. The artifact was materialized FIRST and the existing suite was run against it UNCHANGED, so that the set of controls the new lineage member actually breaks was OBSERVED rather than predicted from a read-only opening. Predicting it is unreliable in this suite: the lineage axis is carried by at least three different predicate shapes - a bare existsSync, a dense-maximum pin with no path literal, and a JSON corpus scan - and a textual sweep for the path literal is blind to the latter two.
FILESYSTEM_SENTINEL_DISPOSITION.WHY_THEY_MUST_MOVE: There is no way to allocate this lineage position without falsifying them. Leaving them would leave the suite red; deleting them would remove the only mechanism that catches an over-allocation.
FILESYSTEM_SENTINEL_DISPOSITION.POSTSTATE: Each existence assertion becomes a POSITIVE EXISTENCE PROOF: existsSync of the v1.0.36 path is TRUE. The predecessor existence proof for v1.0.35 is RETAINED alongside it in every case, so each pair reads as an advance rather than a replacement, and a deletion of either file is caught. The dense maximum advances from 35 to 36. The corpus scan is advanced to the NEXT unallocated pair - version 1.0.37 and HPO-ODS-W2-34 - which preserves its exact shape and its exact purpose while making it true again.
FILESYSTEM_SENTINEL_DISPOSITION.THE_CORPUS_SCAN_IS_ADVANCED_NOT_DELETED: BINDING. The stray-copy predicate is the only control that would catch a second file carrying this version, or an addendum that quietly carries the next grant id. Deleting it to obtain a green would remove the control entirely. It is advanced, both disjuncts together, and remains a scan over every addendum in the directory.
FILESYSTEM_SENTINEL_DISPOSITION.THE_MECHANICALLY_NEXT_ABSENCE_SENTINEL_I: existsSync of docs/ops/ods/ODS_V1_MAINTENANCE_ADDENDUM_v1.0.37.json is asserted FALSE. Without it the lineage axis would carry only positive assertions and a future over-allocation would pass unnoticed.
FILESYSTEM_SENTINEL_DISPOSITION.V1_0_37_IS_NOT_THEREBY_ALLOCATED: Naming v1.0.37 inside an ABSENCE assertion is a PROHIBITION, never an allocation - the identical form v1.0.35 used when it named v1.0.36. An assertion that something does not exist cannot be a claim on it.

THE_HISTORICAL_FROZEN_ASSERTIONS_ARE_LEF.binding: Assertions that record what was true at a PREDECESSOR head - the historical evidence blocks belonging to earlier lanes - are left byte-unchanged even where a live re-reading would now differ.
THE_HISTORICAL_FROZEN_ASSERTIONS_ARE_LEF.why: They are HISTORICAL assertions about a past state, not live assertions about the current one. Advancing them would rewrite evidence rather than advance a sentinel.
THE_HISTORICAL_FROZEN_ASSERTIONS_ARE_LEF.the_distinction_that_matters: A live assertion reads the repository as it is now; a historical assertion pins what a named past act measured. Only the first kind moves.

FILESYSTEM_SENTINEL_DISPOSITION.REGISTRATION_AXIS_SENTINELS_ARE_NOT_TOUC: Every existing control asserting that HPO-ODS-W2-33 is absent from PROTECTED_GRANTS, resolves nowhere, and has zero textual occurrences in scripts/ods-scope.ts remains TRUE and is left exactly as it is. This act allocates the id; it does not register it, so none of those controls changes truth value.
FILESYSTEM_SENTINEL_DISPOSITION.THE_CONTROLLER_AXIS_SENTINELS_ARE_NOT_TO: The assertions that scripts/ods-controller.ts does NOT enumerate v1.0.36 remain TRUE and are left exactly as they are. The Controller is byte-unchanged by this act.

NO_SECOND_LIVE_COUNT_GUARD_IS_INTRODUCED.why: A second live-derived count guard would go RED the moment the registration act adds its row, and would have to be found and advanced by a mission that has no reason to look for it. A literal goes red only where it is meant to.

FILESYSTEM_SENTINEL_DISPOSITION.THE_FROZEN_DECLARED_COUNT_FIGURES_DO_NOT: PROTECTED_GRANTS_COUNT_BEFORE and PROTECTED_GRANTS_COUNT_AFTER are both 20 and both describe the LIVE registry, which this act does not change.
